enums.name: ke_result_domain
enums.doc: The domains that own a range of result codes. A domain's own codes are written `KE_RESULT_CODE(KE_RESULT_DOMAIN_ <DOMAIN >, n)` in its header, with `n` from 1 up.

enums.name: ke_result
enums.doc: What a fallible call returns: `KE_OK`, or the code of the failure. The detail of a failure goes to the failing library's log, never into the code. A caller treats a code it does not know as `KE_RESULT_GENERAL`. Ignoring the result of a call is a compiler warning where the compiler supports it.

enums.name: ke_lifetime
enums.doc: How long the value of an id lasts. A system whose every write has a lifetime shorter than persistent, and that no running system reads within that lifetime, is culled.

values.name: KE_LIFETIME_PERSISTENT
values.doc: The value outlives every run; writing it is an effect no cull removes.

values.name: KE_LIFETIME_PHASE
values.doc: The value lives from the run of the phase it is written in to the end of that run.

values.name: KE_LIFETIME_UNTIL_READ
values.doc: The value lives until every phase whose systems read it has run since it was written. Its writer runs while a system of any phase reads it.

enums.name: ke_phase_cadence
enums.doc: When a phase runs within the ticks of a scheduler.

values.name: KE_PHASE_CADENCE_EVERY_TICK
values.doc: Once per tick, with the tick's dt.

values.name: KE_PHASE_CADENCE_FIXED
values.doc: Once per fixed step, as many steps as the tick's time covers, with the fixed dt. Fixed phases registered one after another run together, in order, at each step.

values.name: KE_PHASE_CADENCE_STARTUP
values.doc: Once, before every other phase of the first tick, with a dt of zero.

values.name: KE_PHASE_CADENCE_SHUTDOWN
values.doc: Once, when the scheduler shuts down after a tick ran, with a dt of zero.

structs.name: ke_input_snapshot
structs.doc: Frozen snapshot of all input state for a single frame. Passed from the input poll to its readers so reads are consistent and thread-safe. The key fields are bitsets. Read them through the snapshot_is_* slots of ke_input rather than indexing them directly; the bit packing is not part of the contract.

fields.name: keys_down
fields.doc: Bitset of keys currently held down.

fields.name: keys_pressed
fields.doc: Bitset of keys that transitioned to down this frame.

fields.name: keys_released
fields.doc: Bitset of keys that transitioned to up this frame.

fields.name: events_dropped
fields.doc: Events lost this frame because the event queue could not grow to hold them.

structs.name: ke_vec2
structs.doc: Two floats, x then y.

structs.name: ke_vec3
structs.doc: Three floats, x then y then z.

structs.name: ke_vec4
structs.doc: Four floats, x then y then z then w.

structs.name: ke_quat
structs.doc: A rotation; the four lanes are x, y, z, w.

structs.name: ke_mat4
structs.doc: Sixteen floats.

structs.name: ke_transform
structs.doc: Spatial transform: where a thing is, how it is turned, and how big it is.

structs.name: ke_variant_table_entry
structs.doc: One authored key and its value. Whoever accepts the key sets `consumed`; the loader reports every entry left unclaimed.

structs.name: ke_component_field
structs.doc: One field of a component: where it lies, what a scene writes into it, and the names an integer field may be written as.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The name a scene writes the field by.

fields.name: default_value
fields.doc: What the field holds when nothing authors it. KE_VARIANT_NULL means the header declared no default and zero stands.

fields.name: enum_names
fields.doc: The names a scene may write for an integer field, in value order; a name stands for its index. None leaves the field numeric.

fields.name: enum_count
fields.doc: Entries in `enum_names`.

structs.name: ke_component_params
structs.doc: What a component type is registered with.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Unique component name.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: Bytes per entity; 0 registers a tag (no storage).

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc: A power of two for a sized component; ignored for a tag of size 0.

fields.name: fields
fields.doc: The type's field layout, normally its field table; copied with every name it reaches, so it only has to live for the call. NULL registers the size alone.

fields.name: field_count
fields.doc: Entries in `fields`; 0 when `fields` is NULL.

structs.name: ke_ecs_segment
structs.doc: One archetype's slice of a query match: the matched entities, plus one column base pointer per query term in the order query_register received them, each aligned 1:1 with `entities`. A tag term's column is NULL. Pointers stay valid until the next structural change.

fields.name: entities
fields.doc: The entities this segment matched.

fields.name: columns
fields.doc: One base pointer per query term.

structs.name: ke_ecs_config
structs.doc: The values an ECS is created with, whatever its implementation, each applied as given.

fields.name: reserved_id_capacity
fields.doc: How many ids entity_reserve may hand out before the world issues any of its own; entity_reserve fails as out of memory once they are spent. Raise it for a world whose systems spawn heavily.

structs.name: ke_id_access
structs.doc: One id a system touches, and how. Two systems conflict when they name the same id and at least one writes it; conflicting systems never run in the same wave.

structs.name: ke_query_desc
structs.doc: A query a system reads through: components matched together, each with its access.

fields.name: terms
fields.doc: The terms the query matches together.

structs.name: ke_phase_desc
structs.doc: A phase: a group of systems run together, wave by wave. A tick runs the phases in the order they were registered, each when its cadence says.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Identifies the phase in diagnostics.

fields.name: cadence
fields.doc: When the phase runs.

fields.name: pipelined
fields.doc: The phase runs on the task pool while the tick goes on and the next one runs; only an every-tick phase can be. Its turn in a tick waits for its previous run, then copies what the queries of its systems match, entities and columns, which is all its bodies read; a body of the phase records no structural change.

structs.name: ke_set_desc
structs.doc: An ordering set: a named anchor of one phase that systems join and that is ordered against other sets of the phase.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Identifies the set in diagnostics.

fields.name: phase
fields.doc: The phase whose systems the set orders.

fields.name: after
fields.doc: Sets of the same phase whose systems all run before this set's.

structs.name: ke_system_desc
structs.doc: A system: a body, the sets it joins and what it touches. It runs in the phase of its sets.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Identifies the system in diagnostics and in the failure its body raises.

fields.name: user_data
fields.doc: Forwarded unchanged to every call of the body.

fields.name: execute
fields.doc: The body.

fields.name: queries
fields.doc: Queries the body reads through ke_scheduler_ctx.view.

fields.name: access
fields.doc: Ids the system touches that no query term covers.

fields.name: sets
fields.doc: The sets the system joins, at least one, all of one phase.

fields.name: per_entity
fields.doc: The body's work on one entity is independent of every other; the scheduler may run it as several concurrent slices of the same entity set.

fields.name: exclusive
fields.doc: The body runs alone at the start of its phase, and what it records is applied before the other systems of the phase run. Its access does not order it.

structs.name: ke_system_order
structs.doc: One system of a phase, as the built order places it.

fields.name: wave
fields.doc: The wave the system runs in; systems of one wave run concurrently.

fields.name: culled
fields.doc: The system does not run: nothing that runs reads what it writes within its lifetime.

structs.name: ke_scheduler_config
structs.doc: What a scheduler is created with, each field applied as given.

fields.name: fixed_dt
fields.doc: The dt of a fixed step, in seconds; greater than zero.

fields.name: fixed_dt_max_accum
fields.doc: The most time a tick may accumulate for fixed steps, in seconds; the excess is dropped; greater than zero.

structs.name: ke_input_actions_config
structs.doc: The values the action maps are created with, whatever its implementation, each applied as given. The values the action maps are created with.

fields.name: section
fields.doc: The configuration section the maps are read from.

fields.name: set
fields.doc: The set the "input.actions" system joins when a scheduler is given; its phase must run before any behaviour reads an action.

slots.name: entity_create
slots.doc: Creates a fresh entity with no components. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

params.name: out_entity
params.doc: Receives the entity; the null entity on failure.

slots.name: entity_destroy
slots.doc: Destroys an entity and all its components; an entity that is not alive is left alone. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for the null entity or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

slots.name: component_register
slots.doc: Registers a component type by name, or returns the existing id if already registered. A repeated name must describe the same size, alignment and layout as its first registration. With `fields` the layouts are compared field by field; without them, only the size and the alignment are compared.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT when the params are missing, the alignment is not a power of two, or the type conflicts with the name's prior registration, what disagrees being logged; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: params
params.doc: The name, size, alignment and field table of the type.

params.name: out_cid
params.doc: Receives the component's id; KE_COMPONENT_INVALID on failure.

slots.name: component_lookup
slots.doc: Looks up a previously registered component by name.
slots.return_doc: false if no component of that name is registered.

params.name: name
params.doc: Component name to find.

params.name: out_meta
params.doc: Receives the component's id, size, and field metadata.

slots.name: component_add
slots.doc: Attaches a component to an entity: its storage is zeroed, then seeded with the defaults of the field table the component was registered with, on the first attach; an entity that already has the component keeps its storage unchanged. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an entity that is not alive, the null entity or component, or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

params.name: out_data
params.doc: Receives the storage, valid until the next structural change on this ecs; NULL for a tag, and on failure.

slots.name: component_remove
slots.doc: Detaches a component from an entity; an entity that is not alive is left alone. Structural; single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for the null entity or component, or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

slots.name: component_get
slots.doc: Returns an entity's component storage, or NULL if it doesn't have that component. The pointer is valid until the next structural change on this ecs.

slots.name: component_size
slots.doc: Byte size of a registered component's element; 0 for a tag or unknown cid.

slots.name: component_field_write
slots.doc: Writes value into component at the place field describes, converted to the field's type: an integer and a float convert to each other, a boolean to an integer, and a vector widens or narrows to the field's width; a string is cut to the field's size and stays NUL-terminated.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a null argument, or for a value that does not convert to the field's type or a size the type cannot have, writing nothing.

params.name: component
params.doc: The component's memory.

params.name: field
params.doc: Where in the component, and of which type and size.

params.name: value
params.doc: The value to write.

slots.name: query_register
slots.doc: Registers a query over a component tuple (entities matching ALL cids).
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an empty tuple, one with more terms than the backend's queries hold, or one the backend refuses, its reason logged; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: cids
params.doc: Component tuple to match.

params.name: cid_count
params.doc: Number of components in the tuple.

params.name: out_query
params.doc: Receives the query; KE_QUERY_INVALID on failure.

slots.name: query_resolve
slots.doc: Resolves a query into archetype segments. MUST run single-threaded, before a parallel wave; afterwards the segments are plain memory touching no backend state.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an unknown query, missing output arrays or a zero capacity, or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged.

params.name: out_segments
params.doc: Receives the matched segments.

params.name: max_segments
params.doc: Capacity of out_segments.

params.name: out_columns
params.doc: Backing store of the segments' columns: segment i's columns are the cid_count entries starting at index i * cid_count, cid_count being the length of the tuple the query was registered with.

params.name: out_count
params.doc: Receives how many segments the query matches; above max_segments, out_segments holds only the first max_segments of them; zero on failure.

slots.name: entity_reserve
slots.doc: Reserves an entity id, callable concurrently from any wave thread — the one entity operation that is. The id is usable immediately as a reference; the entity itself appears in the world when component_add first runs for it, at the wave barrier. An implementation may not satisfy this by forwarding to entity_create, which is single-threaded.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY when every id the implementation can reserve was handed out.

params.name: out_entity
params.doc: Receives the id; the null entity on failure.

slots.name: entity_materialize
slots.doc: Brings a reserved id into the world, so an entity that never receives a component still exists. Structural; single-threaded. A no-op for an id that is already alive or was never reserved.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for the null entity or when the backend refuses the call, its reason logged; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

vtables.name: ke_ecs_commands
vtables.doc: A queue of structural mutations. Every operation records its intent and returns; none changes the world while it runs. The queue is applied, in the order the operations were recorded, by whoever owns it, and an operation's effect is not observable before then. A caller needing a change visible at once uses ke_ecs, which mutates immediately. Recording never touches the world, so these operations may be called while other code reads it. The queue is applied while nothing else runs. An implementation that cannot accept an operation returns its code, logs the reason, and leaves the queue unchanged: KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED in a phase that may not change structure, KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY when the queue cannot grow.

slots.name: spawn
slots.doc: Records the creation of an entity and answers the id it will have. The id can be named by later operations of this queue, and by any caller, at once; the entity itself exists once the queue is applied.

params.name: out_entity
params.doc: Receives the id; KE_ENTITY_INVALID on failure.

slots.name: attach
slots.doc: Records giving `entity` the component `cid`, initialised from `size` bytes of `data`. The bytes are copied, so the caller's buffer need not outlive the call. `size` must equal the registered size of `cid`, or be 0 to attach the component without copying bytes into it.
slots.return_doc: KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT, besides the codes above, when `size` is neither 0 nor the registered size of `cid`.

slots.name: detach
slots.doc: Records removing component `cid` from `entity`.

slots.name: despawn
slots.doc: Records destroying `entity`.

slots.name: defer
slots.doc: Records a structural operation for work the fixed verbs above cannot express. `fn` runs when the queue is applied, in order with the other operations. `user_size` bytes of `user` are copied, so the caller's buffer need not outlive the call.
slots.return_doc: KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT, besides the codes above, for a null `fn`.

vtables.name: ke_scheduler
vtables.doc: Orders systems by what they touch and the sets they join, and runs their phases tick by tick across the task pool.

slots.name: register_phase
slots.doc: Registers a phase.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a missing name, an unknown cadence or a pipelined phase that is not every-tick; KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED from a body; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: out_id
params.doc: Receives the phase's id.

slots.name: register_set
slots.doc: Registers an ordering set.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an unknown phase or a set of `after` from another phase; KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED from a body; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: out_id
params.doc: Receives the set's id.

slots.name: register_system
slots.doc: Registers a system. From a body, it takes effect with the next tick.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a missing name or body, no set, an unknown set or sets of two phases; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: out_id
params.doc: Receives the system's id.

slots.name: unregister_system
slots.doc: Removes a system. From a body, it takes effect with the next tick.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK, or KE_RESULT_NOT_FOUND when no system has that id.

slots.name: declare_lifetime
slots.doc: Declares the lifetime of id; an id never declared is persistent.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an unknown lifetime; KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED from a body; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

slots.name: declare_exclusive
slots.doc: Declares member one of the members of the exclusive group group: no entity holds two members of one group, so queries requiring different members do not conflict.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT when group equals member; KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED from a body; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

slots.name: build
slots.doc: Builds the order of every phase whose registrations changed since the last build; tick builds the same way. Within a phase, the systems of a set run after those of the sets it follows, a writer of an id before its readers, and of two writers with no other order, the one registered first: an ambiguity.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_GENERAL when an order has a cycle or a refused ambiguity, the systems involved named in the log; KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED from a body; KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

params.name: refuse_ambiguity
params.doc: When true, an ambiguity fails the build.

slots.name: describe_phase
slots.doc: The built order of phase, in registration order.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for an unknown phase or too small a capacity; KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED from a body; the code build fails with.

params.name: out_systems
params.doc: Receives one entry per system of the phase.

params.name: out_count
params.doc: Receives the number of systems of the phase.

slots.name: tick
slots.doc: Applies what was recorded into commands, then runs the phases in registration order: on the first tick the startup phases first, then each every-tick phase, and each block of fixed phases once per fixed step the accumulated time covers, the accumulation capped at fixed_dt_max_accum.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a negative dt; KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED from a body or after shutdown; the code build fails with; the code a body or its commands failed with, a body of a pipelined phase's previous run included.

slots.name: flush
slots.doc: Waits for every pipelined phase still running.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED from a body; the code a body of those runs failed with.

slots.name: shutdown
slots.doc: Waits for every pipelined phase still running, then runs the shutdown phases once if a tick ran; a later call, and a later tick, do nothing and are refused respectively. Destroying the scheduler calls it for a caller that did not.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED from a body; the code a body failed with.

slots.name: request_exit
slots.doc: Records that the program should end; any body or the caller may ask, from any thread.

slots.name: exit_requested
slots.doc: Whether a request to end the program was recorded.

slots.name: commands
slots.doc: The queue the caller of tick records structural changes into between ticks; the next tick applies it first. Only the thread that calls tick records into it.
slots.return_doc: The queue, owned by the scheduler.

vtables.name: ke_scheduler_ctx
vtables.doc: What one call of a system body is given: the entities its queries resolved to, its share of them, and the queue it records structural changes into. It means nothing outside the call.

fields.name: commands
fields.doc: The queue the body records structural changes into, applied when its wave ends.

slots.name: view
slots.doc: The resolved segments of the query at query_index, valid for the call.
slots.return_doc: The segments; NULL for an index past the system's queries.

slots.name: slice
slots.doc: Which share of its entity set this call owns: *out_index in [0, *out_count). A system that is not per_entity always gets index 0 of count 1.

vtables.name: ke_input_actions
vtables.doc: Named actions grouped in maps, bound to keys and mouse buttons, evaluated once per frame against an input snapshot and polled. Maps are evaluated from the highest priority down, ties in the order they were added; a key or mouse button bound in an enabled map is not seen by any map evaluated after it. The actions of a disabled map are inactive.

slots.name: add_map
slots.doc: Adds an enabled map after those already present.
slots.return_doc: The map's id; -1 for a null, empty or duplicated name, or when it cannot be stored.

params.name: name
params.doc: Unique among the maps.

params.name: priority
params.doc: Higher is evaluated first.

slots.name: get_map_id
slots.return_doc: The id of the map with that name; -1 when none has it.

slots.name: set_map_enabled
slots.doc: Enables or disables a map from the next evaluation on.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_NOT_FOUND for an id no map has.

slots.name: is_map_enabled
slots.doc: False for an id no map has.

slots.name: get_action_id
slots.return_doc: The id of the action with that name, in any map; -1 when none has it.

slots.name: add_action
slots.doc: Adds an action to a map.
slots.return_doc: The action's id; -1 for an id no map has, a null, empty or duplicated name, or when it cannot be stored.

params.name: name
params.doc: Unique among the actions of every map.

slots.name: bind_key
slots.doc: Adds a key binding to an action.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK; KE_RESULT_NOT_FOUND for an id no action has, or KE_RESULT_OUT_OF_MEMORY.

slots.name: bind_mouse_button
slots.doc: Adds a mouse button binding to an action. Fails as bind_key does.

slots.name: bind_key_pair
slots.doc: Adds a one-axis binding to an action, positive while positive is held and negative while negative is. Fails as bind_key does.

slots.name: bind_key_quad
slots.doc: Adds a two-axis binding to an action: x is right minus left and y is up minus down. Fails as bind_key does.

slots.name: evaluate
slots.doc: Runs one frame of evaluation against snapshot, making each action's held state, edges and axes current.
slots.return_doc: KE_OK, or KE_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a null snapshot, which changes nothing.

callbacks.name: ke_defer_fn
callbacks.doc: A structural operation applied when the queue holding it is drained. `user` points at the copy of the payload passed to defer; `ecs` is the live world. A failure is returned, and the queue stops there: the operations recorded after it are dropped.

callbacks.name: ke_scheduler_execute_fn
callbacks.doc: One call of a system body, once per run of its phase, or once per slice when the system is per_entity. A failure is carried to the thread that called tick, which fails with it; the rest of the wave still runs, and no later wave or phase starts.

lanes.name: ctx
lanes.doc: The body's only doorway to component memory for this call.

lanes.name: dt
lanes.doc: The tick's dt, the fixed dt in a fixed phase, zero at startup and shutdown.
